sections.title: What You'll Learn
sections.content:
Selections let your programs make decisions—just like you do every day! Here’s what we’ll cover:

• How to use `if` statements to choose different actions
• Ways to handle multiple conditions with `else` and `else if`
• How to avoid common mistakes that trip up beginners

sections.title: Core Concepts
Code Examples
Key Points
points: Selection statements allow programs to execute different code based on conditions
Java supports if, if-else, multi-way if-else, and switch for decision making
Conditions are boolean expressions that evaluate to true or false
Selection is essential for making programs respond differently to different inputs
Control flow determines the order in which statements are executed

sections.title: Summary
sections.content: Selections let your program make decisions using `if`, `else if`, and `else`. Conditions must be `boolean` (true/false) expressions. Practice writing conditions for real-world scenarios (like login checks)

questions.question: What is the purpose of selection statements in Java?
options: To repeat a block of code
To make decisions and execute code conditionally
questions.explanation: Selection statements (if, if-else, switch) allow programs to make decisions and execute different blocks of code based on whether conditions are true or false.

questions.question: Which of the following is a selection statement in Java?
questions.explanation: if-else is a selection statement used for making decisions. for, while, and do-while are loop statements used for repetition.
